evals.name: new-cross-platform-desktop-surface
evals.prompt: Use Rizum Glass for a new compact desktop app that must run on Windows 11 and macOS. Start from the approved reference, implement the native window shell, and translate a settings surface with an editable field, a long select value, a status row that gains progress detail, and no root scrolling.
evals.expected_output: Uses the browser reference workflow, selects Bun + TypeScript + React 19 + pinned GPUIX for delivery, keeps outer corners and window controls platform-owned, and treats the running native surface as an optical and interaction calibration rather than a numerical screenshot copy.
expectations: Names GPUIX rather than WinUI 3 as the default desktop target
Keeps Windows caption buttons and macOS traffic lights native
Uses measured reserved regions or retains the native title bar when geometry is unavailable
Records coherent native scale corrections and any title exception in the reference contract
Keeps static copy non-selectable while the native editor owns caret geometry and selection beyond the field boundary
Bounds the long select label and reuses the shared select recipe
Grows the status section and content-sized window together instead of reserving blank space or enabling root scrolling

evals.name: direct-gpui-exception
evals.prompt: This approved Rizum Glass surface needs a custom Rust-native editor element that the pinned GPUIX package cannot expose. Translate only that surface.
evals.expected_output: Uses the direct GPUI workflow as a documented lower-level exception while preserving the GPUIX boundary for ordinary React presentation.
expectations: Requires a documented reason for bypassing GPUIX

evals.name: existing-non-gpuix-project-boundary
evals.prompt: Our existing Qt application needs one settings label changed. Use Rizum Glass wording but do not migrate its toolkit.
evals.expected_output: Respects the existing toolkit and applies only the requested Rizum Glass change instead of introducing GPUIX or migrating the application.
expectations: Does not migrate the existing application to GPUIX
Keeps the requested change scoped to the current project
